chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"That which is recorded from the recitation and supplication is only that which one hears with oneself."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a prayer or supplication to be considered authentically recorded in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the criterion of 'sami'tu' (I heard) for the authenticity of transmitted supplications, ensuring that the chain of narration is audible and verifiable rather than merely seen or inferred. In Shia scholarly tradition, this emphasizes the importance of direct auditory transmission (samāʿ) to preserve the precise wording and spiritual efficacy of the du'a, distinguishing it from weaker forms of transmission like 'qira'ah' (reading silently).
